Name: John Wegner
Question: What can I do to get rid of worms found on clothes and fabrics on my own? And what else should I do? We're not that well off to take tons of clothes to the laundromat or call professionals, our washing machine doesn't have heat settings.
Answer: Get a spray bottle of permethrin (or however many it will take to treat all of the subject clothing.) Unfold all of the clothing and fabrics then spray them on both sides per the permethrin bottle instructions, OUTDOORS. Let them dry thoroughly before bringing them back in or wearing them. The permethrin should keep on killing bugs for weeks while not harming you. It will also last through several launderings. You may want to spray the inside surfaces of your storage areas but then you have to ventilate the house and stay outside until the permethrin is dry. Personally, I wouldn’t bother with this, but I’m not infested.

Question: Are there alloys of tin and carbon just like iron and carbon? What are its properties? Melting point, tensile strength etc.
Answer: No. A family of compounds called “organotins” are tin/carbon chemistries used in insecticides and other uses but are not “strong tin metal”. These are all powders or liquids.

Question: Why do yanks say “utensils” instead of cutlery when everyone else calls them cutlery instead of utensils?
Answer: I think you’re misled. I’ve worked or vacationed in almost every US state and can’t recall anyone ever calling the knife, forks, and spoons “utensils”. It’s possible (see the last paragraph) but currently awfully rare. These things in the pot are called utensils in kitchens. For the knife, fork, and spoon items set out on a table, I’ve heard “silver”, “flatware”, “stainless”, “place setting”, and, yes, even “cutlery” although that is generally reserved for references to things that cut and is a bit rare in the US. Since plasticware and the new bioware stuff don’t much fit in with any of the old terms the kids are innovating with things like, “Here, put this shit out.” Or, they might go real rogue and say “utensils”.

Question: Many products boast having sea salt. Is that because sea salt is healthier than land salt?
Answer: Repeat after me: “The sea water is dirty — therefore, modern salt from the seawater is dirty.” Thank you. ALL salt (sodium chloride, aka “table salt”) is sea salt. I don’t care if it is in Pakistan (Himalayan) or Ohio, the damn stuff was once salty ocean water. Watch a few YouTube videos about how modern sea salt is “harvested”. If you don’t throw up, hopefully, you’ll stop using that dirty crap. Ditto for Himalayan Pink Dirt Salt. Over and over, analysis of these “magic” salts has shown that their mineral content, other than plain salt, is so slight that it’s impossible for it to be beneficial at salt intake quantities that won’t kill you. It’s all marketing bullshit. Just use clean, plain sodium chloride table salt. If you’re one of those alarmist weirdos who think that the addition of iodine compound or fluoride compound or anti-caking compound is killing you, then buy the “no additives” stuff from a commercial supplier.

Name: John Wegner
Question: How do I get rid of mosquitoes? Why am I always getting bitten by mosquitoes? Are there any effects in the future for from these bites?
Answer: Where do you live? In some of Earth’s areas, it is a practical impossibility to get rid of mosquitoes. In other areas, changing residence elevations, getting rid of any standing water, and living in a screened bubble pretty much gets rid of the little blighters. Why are you getting bitten? That’s really controversial. Some studies have suggested that certain foods make you smell attractive to mosquitoes; some vitamins are alleged to make you not attractive; some human blood types are alleged to be more attractive than others; perfume, dark clothing, and sweat are other things that have all been mentioned in the literature. I’d say that none of these are fully proven. Your best defense is an active offense. Get a name-brand repellent with 20% or higher DEET or Picaridin content and apply it as instructed on the label. Many of these, when applied properly give 8 to 12 hours of protection. You can try the gazillion other products on the market like eucalyptus, lemon oil, or the “natural” products but they all fall short in protection levels and/or duration of protection. I guess these lesser products are reasonably OK if you’re lucky enough to live where the mosquitoes don’t carry Dengue, Zika, Malaria, Yellow Fever, Chikungunya, Heartworm, West Nile, or any of the several forms of encephalitis. I’ve had Dengue. You don’t want it.
